newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Products Outlook - Recovery seen after tumble.
newsitem.headline: Asia Products Outlook - Recovery seen after tumble.

text.p: Amid cuts in refinery runs, Asia's diesel and fuel oil prices were expected to stage a mild recovery this week, building on the consolidation seen late last week, traders said on Monday.

They said the undertone for both products remained soft with unsold cargoes overhanging the market, but recent cuts in crude runs at three Singapore refineries would start to clear surplus stocks by the end of the week and help support prices.

Last week, Mobil shut a 45,000 barrels-per-day crude unit at its 280,000 bpd refinery in Jurong, owing to technical problems. Shell Singapore cut runs by around 30,000 bpd at its 435,000 bpd refinery, just more than a week ago.
Esso Singapore cut production 20-25 percent at its 230,000 bpd refinery last weekend.
Singapore Refining said it planned to cut late last week.
After last week's tumble, traders said prices now had more upside potential than downside.
Both gas oil and fuel oil have fallen more than 20 percent in value since the start of the year after a buying spree by China came to a halt and as stocks ballooned in Hong Kong and Singapore.

But by late last week, buyers emerged to support the prices of both products -- after gas oil had dropped below $25.00 per barrel from above $32.00 and after fuel oil had dropped to $93.00 per tone for fuel oil early last week.
Gas oil was assessed Friday at $25.65 and fuel oil 180-cst at $98.00, off lows of the week of $25.35 and $93.00.

Traders said India was likely to add some support to the gas oil market after it awarded over the weekend 615,000 tonnes of high speed diesel in its March tender, and then issued a fresh tender for extra March supplies of 0.5-percent sulphur diesel.
Traders had expected India to award 500,000-600,000 tonnes.

Traders said they expected some support for fuel oil from China, attracted by the low price, and the bunker market, where majors in Singapore reported last week they had run out of January supplies in Singapore.
Jet fuel traders were also bullish saying prices would likely stay strong this week as the current winter has provided good buying support.
Other areas of focus:
* LSWR waiting for final details on Indonesia's February export allocations. Traders expect allocation of around 3.7 million barrels versus January's 3.5 million barrels.
* Korean Electric Power Corp tender to buy two 500,000-barrel cargoes March 11-31 delivery closes January 31, valid one day.
* IOC tender to buy 87 octane leaded gasoline for Feb 21-25 delivery closes January 29, valid one day.
* Taiwan's tender to buy 250,000 barrels of 95-0ctane unleaded reformate March 1-15 delivery closes January 28, valid two days.
* Taiwan's tender to buy two 38,000-tonne cargoes of 0.5 percent sulphur fuel oil for delivery between February and March closes February 3, valid two days.
* India tenders to buy 40-45,000 tonne cargoes of 0.5-pct sulphur diesel for March 1-5 and March 16-20, delivered to Kandla.
